Classical Architecture. Classical Architecture refers to the design principles and structural systems of ancient Greece and Rome, characterized by mathematical proportion, the architectural orders, and emphasis on symmetry. Revived during the Renaissance and systematized through the Enlightenment, it became the dominant language of Western architecture for centuries, codifying rules of proportion and ornament that transcended centuries of building. Rooted in ancient Greek temples and Roman structures like the Pantheon, emphasizing harmonious proportions and structural logic. In addition, built upon the three primary orders - Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian - each with distinct capital designs and ratios; the Composite order fuses Corinthian and Ionic capitals, representing Roman elaboration. Similarly, features load-bearing columns, entablatures (the horizontal beam assembly above columns), and pediments (triangular roof sections); the fluting (vertical grooves) on columns both visually lightens and structurally strengthens them. Another important aspect is that emphasizes bilateral symmetry and the golden ratio, creating a sense of permanence and intellectual order; proportion was understood as divine and mathematical. It's also worth knowing that the trabeated system (post-and-lintel) of columns and beams differs from the arch-and-vault innovations Romans developed, expanding architectural possibilities. Also worth noting is that revived intensively during the Italian Renaissance as architects like Brunelleschi and Palladio studied Roman ruins directly and documented proportional systems. In addition, became the foundation of Neoclassical architecture in the 18th century and remained the norm for civic and institutional buildings into the 20th century; even modernism borrowed classical axial planning and proportional systems. Most notably, the vitruvian principles of firmness (structural soundness), commodity (usefulness), and delight (beauty) unified theory and practice, making classical architecture a comprehensive philosophical system. century revival that made classical grammar the mandatory language of official architecture.
